The ''Junk World''. No one comes to Lotho Minor. ''No one''.''"
"''You're right, kid. No one comes to Lotho Minor—not unless they're crazy.|Brennar and Captain Spikewheel|[[Star Wars Adventures: Return to Vader's Castle 1|''Star Wars Adventures: Return to Vader's Castle'' 1]]}} '''Lotho Minor''', also known as the '''Junk World''', was a ruined [[planet]] in the [[Lotho Minor system]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]' [[Wazta sector]] that was the [[homeworld]] of the mysterious society known as the [[Junker]]s. It was discovered early in the history of the [[Galactic Republic]]. As one of [[the galaxy]]'s dumping grounds, Lotho Minor's surface was covered with [[mountain]]s of trash amassed over untold generations, which brought [[Scavenger|salvage]] operations to the planet in search of machinery that could still be repurposed. Planets such as [[Naboo]] dumped their trash there. Following his defeat at the [[Battle of Naboo]], with his body shattered, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Maul|Darth Maul]] went into [[Exile (punishment)|exile]] in the bowels of Lotho Minor, where he lost his mind. To escape the planet, he sent out a transmission, offering a great sum of [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] for the capture of himself in hopes of luring a [[starship]] that he could escape in. The transmission was intercepted by the [[droid]] [[Captain]] [[Spikewheel]] and her crew of scavenger hopefuls; however, Maul's attempt to flee the planet failed. The crazed [[Sith]] was eventually [[Mission to Lotho Minor|found]] by his brother, [[Savage Opress]], over a [[Standard decade|decade]] after the former's defeat on Naboo. During the [[Galactic Civil War]], the [[Duros]] [[Akar Duel]] ruled over a collection of [[monster droid]]s built from Lotho Minor's scrap and claimed the planet as his own, but his servants turned against him and [[Manumission|gained]] their freedom following an encounter with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] [[3PO-series protocol droid|droid]] [[C-3PO]]. ==Description== {{Quote|We've got everything here!|Morley, in reference to Lotho Minor's junk fields|audio=Lotho_Minor_2.flac|}} [[File:Lotho_Minor.png|thumb|right|340px|Lotho Minor was a deadly and desolate planet located in the Outer Rim.]] A stormy, desolate terrestrial [[planet]] in [[orbit]] of the [[Star|sun]] [[Lotho]], Lotho Minor was located beyond the [[Western Reaches]] in the [[Lotho Minor system]], which itself was located in the northern part of the [[Outer Rim Territories]]' [[Wazta sector]], in grid square I-17 on the [[Standard Galactic Grid]]. The world was close to the [[Koda Spur]] [[hyperspace route]], which connected it to the planet''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' [[Thune]] and a [[space station]] known as [[Koda Station]]. Lotho Minor had a [[Color|brownish]] surface covered with enormous [[mountain]]s of trash piled over countless generations, with much of it permanently on [[fire]], and had more junk than even the planet [[Raxus Prime]]. No [[approach vector]]s that could be used to enter the [[atmosphere]] were established. The gutted and rotting [[hull]]s of ancient [[starship]]s poked through the more recent garbage, lending its landscape the eerie feel of an industrial graveyard. Foul-smelling fog limited visibility, while huge pools of toxic sludge and periodic bursts of [[Death|deadly]]''[[Servants of the Empire: The Secret Academy]]'' [[acid rain]] made the [[Temperature|hot]] and caustic planet's ruined ecosystem one of the most dangerous in [[the galaxy]]. The planet's Type I atmosphere was breathable to some [[species]], yet Lotho Minor looked rusty and unattractive even from orbit, featuring occasional and aggressive rains of solid [[metal]] along with strong winds that blew the junk across the world. Combined with [[rust storm]]s, underground explosions, and other sudden movements in the lower layers, Lotho Minor's numerous planetary hazards provoked the detachment of sharp waste and debris or flash floods of chemicals previously held by weather-worn dams. "[[Left tunnel|Nellis Express to Lotho Minor]]" was the nickname for a deadly tunnel in the [[Safa Toma Speedway]], a [[Riot Racing]] track{{TBB|Faster}} located on the planet [[Serolonis]]{{SW|url=faster-trivia-gallery|text="Faster" Trivia Gallery | The Bad Batch}} {{C|Slide 6}} around the [[Standard year|year]] [[19 BBY]],{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-bad-batch-season-2-trailer-key-art|text=Clone Force 99 Is Back in New ''Star Wars: The Bad Batch'' Season 2 Trailer|date=2022-12-07}} dates the events of the [[The Bad Batch Season 2|second season]] of ''[[Star Wars: The Bad Batch]]'', which includes "[[Faster]]," to [[Standard month|months]] after the [[attack on Kamino]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' places in [[19 BBY]]. in reference to the likewise-dangerous Lotho Minor. The planet also contained pits, which were the subject of [[List of phrases and slang|slang]] used as an interjection for surprise: "What in the pits of Lotho Minor?" The [[smuggler]] [[Han Solo]] uttered the phrase upon confronting infant [[sarlacc]]s that could move around[[Galaxy's Edge 1|''Galaxy's Edge'' 1]] around [[5 BBY]].''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' ==History== ===Galactic dumping ground=== {{Quote|Fire-breathers. They'll getcha!|Morley, to Savage Opress|audio=Lotho_Minor_5.flac|}} [[File:LothoMinorJunk-TCW.jpg|thumb|left|340px|Lotho Minor became an official dumping ground shortly after its discovery.]] Despite being located beyond the very remote Western Reaches, Lotho Minor was discovered in the early [[Standard day|days]] of the [[Galactic Republic]]. It was quickly designated as a junk repository after the discovery that very few [[Sentience|sentient]] species were [[Homeworld|indigenous]] to the planet—the few that were did not matter to the Republic's self-interested [[Politics|politicians]] or corporations. While the Republic initially tried to control the traffic destined for Lotho Minor with the help of several large mega-corporations, the lack of a permanent presence or Republic [[Realspace|space]] station that could be used to patrol the surface allowed anyone wishing to leave their waste on the planet's surface to do so, forcing inhabitants to be careful of falling debris, which blended into the rest of the once-harmless planet. The species that did consider Lotho Minor their home [[Merchant|traded]] with some of the few visitors to the world. Eventually, the planet [[Naboo]] came to send its untreatable waste and contaminated [[coolant]] there through an automatic refill system,{{EncyclopediaCite|Naboo}} and [[drone barge]]s ferried junk from the [[moon]] [[Cymoon 1]] to Lotho Minor.{{BuildFalconCite|78|Guide to the Galaxy}} [[Freighter|Cargo ships]] routinely dropped holds of garbage onto the planet with little concern for neither what became of it{{Databank|fire-breather|Fire-breather}} nor any security measures, often doing so without warning. [[Standard century|Centuries]] before the [[Clone Wars]], immense [[refuse incinerator droid]]s were [[Programmer|programmed]] to incinerate Lotho Minor's garbage. As centuries went on, Lotho Minor's pollution drove all of its few sentient species to extinction. While most non-native species equated Lotho Minor to [[Chaos|Hell]], it was considered a legendary haven by [[Jawa]]s, [[Squib]]s, and [[Ugor]]s. [[File:FirebreatherLothoMinor-TCWS04E21.jpg|thumb|right|305px|Enormous "fire-breathers" incinerated the mountains of scrap on Lotho Minor.]] Due to the horrible conditions that made Lotho Minor one of the most dangerous planets in the [[galaxy]], cultural [[historian]]s, [[archaeologist]]s, and students of [[engineer]]ing history could not conduct researches to find answers to their questions. [[Junk dealer]]s from throughout the Outer Rim traveled to the planet to [[Scavenger|scavenge]] functional parts among countless layers of junk on Lotho Minor's surface. Since [[radiation]] spikes made scanning difficult, visitors were forced to fly their vessels very low while trying not to be beaten down by a rain of debris transformed into [[meteorite]]s—a fate shared by many. A number of the more careful junk dealers chose to engage with Lotho Minor's population of [[Junker]]s. By [[20 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of "[[Brothers (episode)|Brothers]]," which features the [[Refuse incinerator droid|fire-breathers]] on Lotho Minor, to [[20 BBY]]. the refuse incinerator droids continued to labor among the mountains of garbage. Those unfortunate enough to live on Lotho Minor did not know the [[droid]]s' origins and referred to them simply as "fire-breathers." Salvage operations also dug through the planet-wide junkyard, looking to reclaim and recondition reusable or obsolete machinery, and Lotho Minor came to be known as the Junk World. ===Darth Maul's exile=== {{Quote|This is where you live? How long have you been here?''"
"''Years and years and years.|Savage Opress and Darth Maul|audio=Lotho_Minor_3.flac|}} [[File:LothoTrial-ReturnToVadersCastle1.jpg|thumb|left|305px|Captain Spikewheel stranded a group of recruits on Lotho Minor to capture Darth Maul.]] After his defeat at the hands of the [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] during the [[Battle of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY]], the shattered body of [[Maul|Darth Maul]], a [[Dathomirian]] [[Zabrak]] [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]], was dumped amid Lotho Minor's junk via a container of waste [[water]] delivered from Naboo. As his sanity waned,{{EncyclopediaCite|Darth Maul and Other Followers of the Dark Side}} Maul lived in [[Exile (punishment)|hiding]] for more than a [[Standard decade|decade]] in the [[cave]]s beneath Lotho Minor's surface, subsisting off trash{{SWE|characters|morley|Morley}} and vermin, but his driving desire to cling to life pushed him to rebuild himself with [[spider]]-like [[Limb|legs]] made of the planet's scrap metal{{HelmetCollectionCite|14|Weapons & Uniforms}} in place of his [[Dismemberment|severed]] ones. At one point, Maul was attacked by Lotho Minor's vermin, eventually killing one of the [[insect]]s and [[Diet|eating]] it raw, and also destroyed a fire-breather processing machine by hurling his [[Darth Maul's double-bladed lightsaber|lightsaber]] into it. An [[Anacondan]] named [[Morley]] pulled Maul into his lair out of curiosity, presuming he would make a good meal, but was proven otherwise. Morley instead cut a deal with Maul in order to survive,{{Databank|morley|Morley}} agreeing to lure unwitting prey into Maul's clutches in return for his leftovers. At some point, Maul attempted to escape Lotho Minor by luring a starship that he could escape in. He sent out a transmission that offered a large amount of [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] for capturing him. The transmission would eventually be heard by [[Spikewheel]], the droid [[captain]] of the starship ''[[Salvage-1]]'', who traveled to the planet a [[Standard week|week]] later. She stranded the [[Kadas'sa'Nikto|Nikto]] [[Gritz]], who aspired to become the droid's [[First Mate|first mate]] and was tasked with capturing Maul, along with three other crew member hopefuls—the [[human]] [[Brennar]], the [[Theelin]] [[Riki]], and the [[Roonan]] [[Seles]]—to serve as bait. Not long after Spikewheel left the group on the planet surface, they fell into Maul's [[Darth Maul's lair|subterranean lair]] subsequent to a quick scuffle with each other. [[File:MaulHunts-ReturnToVadersCastle1.jpg|thumb|right|210px|Seles is captured by Maul in the latter's lair.]] With the group trying to find their way within the dark labyrinth, Maul quietly grabbed Seles and separated him from the rest of the recruits, but Brennar soon found both Maul and the captured Roonan. As the duo was about to be killed by the insane Zabrak, Gritz managed to ensnare Maul in an [[Stun net|electronet]] and save them. The recruits later returned to Spikewheel with the captured Zabrak aboard the ''Salvage-1''. Before the ship could leave the planet's atmosphere, Maul freed himself and attacked the scavengers, splitting the droid captain in half. Riki subsequently opened the ship's rear hatch to ditch Maul; however, Gritz and the remains of his captain also fell from the ship along with Maul during the process, leaving the hapless [[Nikto]] to be killed by Maul while the other recruits escaped the planet. Years later, [[Vaneé]], the [[Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader's]] [[Aide|attendant]], told the story of the salvagers to scare his [[prisoner]], [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebel]] [[Lieutenant]] [[Thom Hudd]], at [[Fortress Vader|Vader's castle]]. ===Brothers reunited=== {{Quote|The cargo you just dropped off, what planet did it come from?''"
"''The junk fields on planet Lotho Minor!|Savage Opress and a cargo hauler|audio=Lotho_Minor_1.flac|}} [[File:MaulsLair-Brothers.png|thumb|left|320px|Savage Opress finds his lost brother, Darth Maul, beneath the surface of Lotho Minor.]] Lotho Minor remained neutral during the Clone Wars, and in 20 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]], [[Mother (title)|Mother]] [[Talzin]] of the [[Dathomir]]ian [[Nightsisters]] tasked [[Savage Opress]] with finding Maul, his long-lost brother, and gave him the [[Talisman of Finding]] to aid in his quest.{{TCW|Witches of the Mist}} On the planet [[Stobar]], the talisman guided Opress to some dust clinging to an assortment of cargo crates that were being [[transport]]ed by a [[Unidentified Sakiyan cargo hauler|Sakiyan cargo hauler]]. Opress learned that the [[Sakiyan]]'s [[TR-RL3 Terrapin-class bulk tanker|Turtle Tanker]] had recently visited Lotho Minor and forced the hauler to take him there. When they arrived, Opress dropped the Sakiyan out of the ship in mid-air. While [[Mission to Lotho Minor|scouring]] the planet's endless garbage wastes for his brother, Opress encountered Morley, who guided him past such threats as the enormous fire-breathers and a tribe{{SWE|groups|junkers|Junkers}} of territorial Junkers, some of who were slain by the Zabrak. Morley lured Opress into Maul's lair, believing Lotho Minor's newest guest would be their next [[Foodstuff|meal]]. At first, the two [[Maul's family|brothers]] wrestled with each other in the dark labyrinth of garbage, but Opress quickly recognized Maul and saw that his brother's mind had been shattered by his long-ago defeat. When Morley interrupted them to check on the status of their meal, Opress strangled the Anacondan to death for his treachery. At Opress' prodding, Maul soon remembered himself and vowed revenge on the Jedi. The brothers then traveled back to the world Dathomir, where Talzin repaired Maul's body and mind.{{TCW|Revenge (episode)}} ===Planet of misfit droids=== {{Quote|I was going to say, your ship is junk—magnificent, beautiful junk. And on this planet—''my'' planet…we crave junk. We must have it.|Akar Duel appreciates the ''Millennium Falcon''|}} [[File:Lotho_Minor_rebels.jpg|thumb|right|295px|Akar Duel and his droids confront the rebels.]] By the [[time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War]] between the [[Galactic Empire]] and the Rebel Alliance, a [[Duros]] named [[Akar Duel]] had come to consider Lotho Minor his own planet. He created many [[Monster droid|junk droids]] from the droid parts he collected on the planet and used [[restraining bolt]]s to force them into his service. Sometime after the [[Battle of Yavin]], a [[Heroes of Yavin|team]] of rebels consisting of [[Luke Skywalker]], Han Solo, [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]], [[Chewbacca]], and the [[3PO-series protocol droid|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO]] traveled to Lotho Minor aboard the [[YT-1300 light freighter|starship]] ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'' in search of a suitable location for a new base. Two of Duel's droids, [[Doc]] and [[Teetee]], attempted to warn the rebels about the Duros, but he had already noticed their arrival. Surrounding the rebels with his conscripted droids, Duel wanted to [[Thief|steal]] the ''Millennium Falcon''; however, the droids turned against their master upon learning that C-3PO was allowed to have free will, unlike themselves, and they eventually [[Manumission|gained]] their freedom. The rebels then quickly fled Lotho Minor, giving up the idea of establishing a base there. Sometime later, after leaving the planet themselves, Doc and Teetee told their story to [[Bazine Netal]], a [[spy]] who was searching for the ''Millennium Falcon''. Another droid that found its way to Lotho Minor was a [[Team Slingshot droideka|droideka]] that was at some point discovered by the [[Ugnaught]] [[Dizzy (Ugnaught)|Dizzy]]. Enthralled by the idea of the great speeds a machine like it could reach, Dizzy took ownership of the droid and heavily modified it. While on the planet, the Ugnaught also took the time to cobble together a [[Racer|racing]] [[Clothing|suit]] based on material found on Lotho Minor, deciding not to be picky when it came to the options available. Dizzy and the [[droideka]] later entered the [[Hunters of the Outer Rim]], a tournament held on the planet [[Vespaara]]''[[Star Wars: Hunters]]'' in [[9 ABY]], going by the united persona of [[Slingshot (team)|Slingshot]].{{Hunters|url=characters/slingshot|text=Slingshot}} ===Wreck Belt ordeals and shady trades=== {{Quote|You sssshould have ''left'' me on that frossst planet—at least it was ssssafer than thissss place, ''T'onga''.|Bossk, while orbiting Lotho Minor|[[Bounty Hunters 20|''Bounty Hunters'' 20]]}} [[File:WreckBelt-BountyHunters20.png|thumb|left|300px|A debris field known as the Wreck Belt orbited Lotho Minor.]] The [[assassin droid]]s [[0-0-0]] and [[BT-1]] traveled to the [[Wreck Belt]] orbiting Lotho Minor in [[0 ABY]], shortly after the former lost his original arms at the [[Battle of Vrogas Vas]].[[Star Wars (2015) 13|''Star Wars'' (2015) 13]] For receiving repair and supplies, the droids visited a [[Ruen's workshop|workshop]] at the Belt, which was operated by a human [[mercenary]] [[technician]] named [[Ruen]]. While 0-0-0 was undergoing repairs, Ruen noticed that the droid carried a valuable [[Triple-Zero protocol personality matrix|personality matrix]] and attempted to steal it. As BT-1 halted Ruen's plans and threated to kill him, the two parties eventually agreed on leaving on good terms after the mechanic fulfilled the original deal. However, before leaving the workshop, BT-1 hacked into the shop's systems and granted Ruen's [[Battle droid|combat droids]] their independence. The droids soon turned against Ruen and killed him, detonating the entire workshop in the process. Years later, around [[3 ABY|3]]–[[4 ABY]],The events of [[Bounty Hunters 20|''Bounty Hunters'' 20]] take place between the [[War of the Bounty Hunters]] and the events of {{Film|VI}}, which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[3 ABY]] and [[4 ABY]], respectively. the droid [[bounty hunter]] [[4-LOM]], having been reprogrammed and given a deadly new body, laid a trap in a derelict [[Hutt freighter]] located at Lotho Minor's Wreck Belt for his former partner, the [[Gand]] [[Zuckuss]]. Knowing he was walking into a trap but desperate to reunite with his only friend, Zuckuss traced the droid's signal and traveled to the Belt with a [[T'onga's crew|party]] of four other hunters—[[T'onga]], [[Losha Tarkon]], [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]], and [[Tasu Leech]]—aboard the starship [[Edgehawk (starship)|''Edgehawk'']]. Upon boarding the derelict ship, the team confronted the [[bounty]] droid, with Zuckuss disconnecting 4-LOM's head from his body and resetting the droid's personality. [[File:Halcyon-GalacticStarcruiserConceptArt.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A passenger aboard the ''Halcyon'' (pictured) haggled for a crate from Lotho Minor.]] In [[34 ABY]],{{TravelersGuidetoBatuuDate}} the historian and [[author]] [[Eloc Throno]] marked Lotho Minor's location in a galaxy [[map]] published in his [[book]] ''[[Traveler's Guide to Batuu]]''.''[[Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge: Traveler's Guide to Batuu]]'' That same year,''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Galactic Starcruiser|''Star Wars'': Galactic Starcruiser]] to [[34 ABY]]. a passenger aboard the ''[[Halcyon]]'' [[Star Cruiser|starcruiser]] was contacted by [[Tohago]], assistant to the [[collector]] [[Dok-Ondar]], regarding a request for antiquities. The passenger asked Tohago if they could take some crates from Lotho Minor—likely filled with junk—off{{DatapadCite|Comms: Tohago|Tohago-SCDatapadComms.jpg|gs=yes}} her''[[Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge: Traveler's Guide to Batuu]]'' hands. The assistant originally declined, stating the crates were not for sale and that her employer would not let go of them lightly, but the passenger persisted, and Tohago caved, offering the lot of crates up for 15,000 credits. The passenger haggled for a single crate, and the assistant settled the deal with 6,000 credits, receiving her payment from the [[Saja]], a [[The Force|Force]] [[Religion|sect]] from the{{DatapadCite|Comms: Saja|SajaComms1-Datapad.png|gs=yes}} [[moon]]''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' [[Jedha]]. ==Inhabitants== {{Quote|Trust me! Not everything on this planet is junk.''"
"''It's not?''"
"''There are things like me. Things that live and breathe.|Morley and Savage Opress|audio=Lotho_Minor_4.flac|}} [[File:Junkers.jpg|thumb|left|325px|Lotho Minor's native Junkers survived on the planet's scrap and augmented their bodies with cybernetic enhancements.]] Lotho Minor was the homeworld of the mysterious Junkers, although their population was small. Consisting of various species,''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]'' the tribal denizens appeared to be a strange hybrid of organic life and mechanical debris, and no one was quite sure of their origin. Lotho Minor's role as a galactic dumping ground and the Junkers' violent territoriality discouraged any deep exploration into their culture or biology. The Junkers lived off the scrap found on their homeworld's surface, augmenting their twisted bodies with [[Cybernetics|cybernetic]] enhancements, which replaced their missing limbs that were lost to corrosive chemicals, radiation, or accidents.{{BuildR2Cite|52|Droid Directory}} They had lived on Lotho Minor for so long that it was impossible to tell where their bodies ended and the garbage began. Other [[Microscope|microscopic]] natives to the world were exterminated [[Millennium|millennia]] prior to the Clone Wars, with yet other creatures having been present for a number of centuries and thus were considered endemic. [[File:Slingshot-SWHunters.png|thumb|right|270px|A droideka resided on Lotho Minor until being recovered by the Ugnaught Dizzy.]] The Junk World was also the homeworld of the cunning Anacondan Morley during the Clone Wars. The [[Snake|serpentine]] creature slithered through the mountains of trash and survived by delivering sustenance to [[Darth]] Maul in exchange for the exiled Sith Lord's scraps. While the debris of galactic civilization on Lotho Minor lay largely inactive,''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]'' the world's population additionally included individuals whose ships had crashed and therefore were trying to find a way offworld; those who had committed atrocities would also sometimes find their way to Lotho Minor to go into hiding. Individuals hoping to find precious metals were another group that resided on the planet. During the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the Empire, the Duros Akar Duel lived on Lotho Minor and regarded himself as the planetary ruler. He employed many junk droids by force, including Doc, Teetee, and [[Unidentified junk droid (EV unit)|another droid]] with the head of an [[EV-series]] unit. In a life-changing moment for all the droids on Lotho Minor, Duel's servants revolted against their master and gained their freedom. A droideka also spent time on the world before being taken away by the Ugnaught Dizzy. ==Locations== {{Quote|There's a ''haunted labyrinth'' beneath all that scrap.|Captain Spikewheel|}} Beneath the enormous piles of trash on Lotho Minor's surface, the Sith Lord Darth Maul lived in a cavernous lair during his exile. Accessible through a deep pit inside a shelter on the surface, Maul's lair consisted of deep tunnels in the junk. Lotho Minor was orbited by a mechanical debris field known as the Wreck Belt, where the mechanic Ruen operated his workshop. ==Behind the scenes== ===Appearance and conception=== {{Quote|I was a huge fan of the ''Clone Wars'' series long before I got this project, and I was familiar with the look of planet Lotho Minor, but for the story I went back to closely examine the world as it's depicted in the episode 'Brothers.' To keep the junkyard setting from overpowering the characters and their action, I took a cue from the series' design choice to show the piles of junk and debris as vague, jagged shapes. It doesn't really take a lot of detail to suggest that these are mountain ranges made up of years and years of garbage pileup, ready to topple over on themselves or crush anyone who disturbs them.|Megan Levens|{{SW|url=news/behind-the-spooky-scenes-of-idws-return-to-vaders-castle-1-exclusive|text=Behind the Spooky Scenes of IDW's ''Return to Vader's Castle'' #1 - Exclusive|author=[[Dan Brooks|Brooks, Dan]]|date=2019-10-01}}}} [[File:Lotho_Minor_Spirit_Of_B.jpg|thumb|right|355px|Lotho Minor environment design illustration by Pat Presley]] Lotho Minor was created for "[[Brothers (episode)|Brothers]]," the twenty-first episode in the [[The Clone Wars: Season Four|fourth season]] of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' animated television series, which first aired on [[March 9]], [[2012]].''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Episode Guide]]'' Several "spirit of" designs for Lotho Minor were illustrated by [[Kilian Plunkett]] and [[Pat Presley]], and the planet was referred to as "Lamoth" in some pieces of concept art.{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/brothers-concept-art-gallery|text="Brothers" Concept Art Gallery}} {{C|Slides 5, 6, 9, and 10}} The [[StarWars.com]] [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|Encyclopedia]] entry for Lotho Minor introduced the nickname "Junk World." Lotho Minor was originally introduced in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity via the young-adult novel ''[[The Wrath of Darth Maul]]'', written by [[Ryder Windham]]''[[The Wrath of Darth Maul]]'' and released in [[January]] 2012. This story referenced the events of the ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' episode "Brothers"''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' prior to its television debut. Information on Lotho Minor was included in [[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 62|sixty-second issue]] of [[De Agostini]]'s ''[[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon]]'' magazine, published around [[March]] 9, [[2016]].{{BMFdates|62}} The section mentioning the planet was written by [[Tim Veekhoven]] as part of the assorted lore he was able to introduce while writing for the magazine run.{{DMCite|dm=File:TimVeekhoven-Credits.png|creator=Tim Veekhoven}} The planet later appeared in a story dubbed "The Horned Devil!" in the [[Star Wars Adventures: Return to Vader's Castle 1|first issue]] of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]] ''[[Star Wars Adventures: Return to Vader's Castle]]'', which was written by [[Cavan Scott]] with art by [[Megan Levens]], and was released by [[IDW Publishing]] on [[October 2]], [[2019]]. As preparation for her task, Levens examined Lotho Minor's depiction in "Brothers," patterning her illustration on the episode's design choice to show the planet's piles of junk and debris as vague, jagged shapes, suggesting that they consisted of unsteady garbage piled up over many years. She also indicated that she imagined the environment of the sinkhole and tunnels beneath the surface of Lotho Minor as the carcass of an old structure or ship that had decayed under centuries of heavy garbage and environmental stress, designing the tunnels as they were either former corridors or giant ducts. Lotho Minor also appeared in the [[Star Wars video games|mobile video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'', developed by [[EA Capital Games]]''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'' and first released on [[November 24]], [[2015]].{{SW|url=news/how-to-become-a-master-of-the-holotables-in-star-wars-galaxy-of-heroes|text=How to Become a Master of the Holotables in ''Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes''|nolive=1}} The planet's enviroment for the game was almost exclusively modeled by Lead Environment Artist [[Sean Buck]].{{WebCite|url=https://www.seanbuck3d.com/star-wars-goh|text=STAR WARS: GALAXY OF HEROES|author=[[Sean Buck]]|archivedate=20250926132605}} Additionally, the mobile game ''[[Star Wars: Hunters]]'', which was initially published by [[Zynga]] on [[November 16]], [[2021]], as a [[Wikipedia:Soft launch|soft launch]]{{Twitter|ZyngaStarWars|status/1460656552734605317|[[Zynga]] Star Wars|date=2021-11-16|quote=We are excited to announce Star Wars: Hunters is now entering soft launch and is available on Android for players in India, Philippines, Malaysia & Indonesia.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/InyRJ|archivefile=File:ZyngaStarWars-SoftLaunchDate-Twitter.png}} before the global release on [[June 4]], [[2024]],{{SWYouTube|4dZcq6m3y40|Star Wars: Hunters Launch Date Reveal Trailer}} featured an unlockable cosmetics item titled "Lotho Racing Green" for Dizzy's droideka as part of the playable character duo Slingshot in the game. The item painted the destroyer in muddied yellows, greens, and brownsmakes, referring to Lotho Minor's surface aesthetic. The game closed on on [[October 1]], [[2025]].{{Hunters|url=news/sunset-on-vespaara|text=Sunset on Vespaara}} ===Inconsistencies=== [[File:LothoMinorBunker-SpiritOf.jpg|thumb|left|335px|Concept art for "Lotho Minor bunker" by Kilian Plunkett]] While the sixty-second issue of the ''Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon'' magazine places Lotho Minor in grid square I-7 of the Standard Galactic Grid as part of the Wazta [[sector]], the [[2020]] ''[[Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge: Traveler's Guide to Batuu]]'' and the 2021 ''[[Star Wars Droids Guide to a Galaxy Far, Far Away]]'' both place the planet in''[[Star Wars Droids Guide to a Galaxy Far, Far Away]]'' what [[Star Wars: The Force Awakens Beginner Game|''Star Wars: The Force Awakens'' Beginner Game]] identifies as grid square I-17.[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens Beginner Game|''Star Wars: The Force Awakens'' Beginner Game]] Since [[Christopher Ibbitt]]'s{{EmailCite|email=File:AtlasEmail-2025-07-31.png|creator=[[Jason Fry]]|date=2025-07-31}} [[2022]] [[Star Wars Galaxy Map (poster)|''Star Wars'' Galaxy Map]] also places Lotho Minor in I-17, this article assumes the aforementioned ''Build the Millennium Falcon'' issue is erroneous. The same ''Build the Millennium Falcon'' issue also establishes that Lotho Minor was situated on the [[Lutrillian Cross]], adding that it was the closest and largest [[hyperspace]] route to the Lotho Minor [[Star system|system]]. This contradicts the route's placement{{BuildFalconCite|18|Guide to the Galaxy}} relative to the planet's location on the ''[[Star Wars]]'' Galaxy Map. This article treats the information from ''Build the Millennium Falcon'' as an error. ''Build the Millennium Falcon'' 62 also suggests that few beings visited the world's surface, which creates an apparent contradiction with "[[Hoth and Other Planets in the Outer Rim]]," the fifty-ninth issue of De Agostini's [[Star Wars Encyclopedia (series)|''Star Wars Encyclopedia'']] reference booklets released on [[January 12]], 2022.{{Altaya|lang=fr|url=livres-bd/encyclopedie-star-wars|text=Encyclopédie Star Wars}} The issue states that junk dealers from all over the Outer Rim Territories were known to travel to the world. This article disregards the information provided by the former source. An apparent contradiction exists related to Lotho Minor's location relative to the Western Reaches. ''Build the Millennium Falcon'' 62 establishes that the world was situated on the "edge" of that region, whereas the book ''[[Star Wars: The Galactic Explorer's Guide]]'' by [[Jason Fry]],''[[Star Wars: The Galactic Explorer's Guide]]'' released on [[December 20]], 2019,{{BN|url=w/star-wars-jason-fry/1132547716|text=Star Wars: The Galactic Explorer's Guide}} {{C|US}} instead places the area of space that corresponds to Lotho Minor's grid square in the Western Reaches.
